purpose: Canonical, machine-readable completion semantics for the nine engineering-quality runner paths. This file is the SINGLE source; docs/producer-completion-contracts.md is generated from it and never maintained beside it.

reading_rules.current_process_observation: what the SHIPPED runner captures about the process. 'unobserved' means the status is discarded at the call site; it does NOT mean the tool's semantics are unknown.
reading_rules.current_report_observation: what can be inferred from the produced report. A parseable report proves REPORT READABILITY ONLY - never full target coverage or successful execution, unless report_finalization_condition establishes it.
reading_rules.upstream_exit_semantics: what the tool's own exit codes mean. 'unknown' is recorded with the missing source named, and is a different fact from the runner discarding the status.
reading_rules.normative_completion_requirement: what C2 must observe before granting completed-analysis credit.

producers.backend_selection: executable probe: SENTINEL_SHIELD_INFECTION_BIN, else vendor/bin/infection, else infection on PATH

current_process_observation.mechanism: the invocation ends in `|| true`; the process status is discarded at the call site

current_report_observation.condition: the Infection JSON logger parses and .stats.msi is numeric
current_report_observation.does_not_prove: that the mutation run covered the full target, or that it terminated normally

upstream_exit_semantics.known: the runner passes --min-msi=0 SPECIFICALLY so Infection never fails the process on a low score; the threshold decision belongs to Sentinel via quality.mutation.min_score. Established from shipped code, so this part is a repository-owned contract.
upstream_exit_semantics.unknown: which exit codes Infection uses for infrastructure failure versus completion
upstream_exit_semantics.missing_source: no composer.lock / package-lock.json in this repository: these are consumer-side dev dependencies, so no pinned version exists here whose documented exit table could be cited

producers.normative_completion_requirement: An observed process outcome separating a completed mutation run from one aborted, killed or timed out after flushing a partial JSON logger. A present .stats.msi is NOT sufficient.

timeout_handling.note: no bounded-process wrapper; a timeout kill is indistinguishable from completion at the call site

report_finalization_condition.note: no authoritative signal that the logger is complete rather than truncated

analyzed_scope_identity.note: the runner does not record which files were mutated

configuration_identity.note: the threshold is read but no digest is bound to the evidence

target_commit_binding.note: ne_target_json binds repository/commit when CI supplies them

record_report_binding.required: the record must carry the sha256 of the report AS WRITTEN, so a stale successful record cannot be paired with a newer failed run

no_observation_behavior.matrix: unobserved -> never valid-clean; findings surface as valid-findings-unobserved

producers.residual_gap: C2 must wrap the invocation so exit status, signal and timeout are captured, and must define a finalization condition for the Infection logger.

producers.backend_selection: knip first when node_modules/.bin/knip is executable; otherwise ts-prune from node_modules/.bin or PATH. Selected at run time, and the choice CHANGES THE COUNTING SEMANTICS.

current_process_observation.knip: unobserved - the knip invocation ends in `|| true`
current_process_observation.ts-prune: OBSERVED - a ts-prune failure is caught and leaves the report absent rather than producing a clean one

current_report_observation.condition: knip: .files and .issues arrays present, every issue category summed. ts-prune: line count excluding '(used in module)'.
current_report_observation.does_not_prove: comparability between the two backends - knip sums issue categories, ts-prune counts output lines, so one producer key can carry two non-comparable numbers

upstream_exit_semantics.missing_source: no composer.lock / package-lock.json in this repository: these are consumer-side dev dependencies, so no pinned version exists here whose documented exit table could be cited

producers.normative_completion_requirement: An observed outcome per backend, AND the backend identity recorded in the evidence: a knip->ts-prune switch changes what the number means and can happen between CI runs purely by dependency installation.

signal_handling.note: a ts-prune signal death is caught by its failure guard; a knip signal death is not

configuration_identity.source: none - dead_code has no numeric threshold

record_report_binding.required: sha256 of the report as written, PLUS the backend that produced it

no_observation_behavior.matrix: unobserved -> never valid-clean; findings surface as valid-findings-unobserved

producers.residual_gap: Backend identity is not recorded anywhere in the evidence, so a knip result and a ts-prune result are indistinguishable to a consumer. C2 must record it as provenance.

producers.backend_selection: executable probe: vendor/bin/pest first, else vendor/bin/phpunit; overridable by env

current_process_observation.mechanism: the exit status IS captured into a local variable, then only logged; it never reaches the evidence

current_report_observation.condition: the Clover file exists and is non-empty, then the adapter produces the normalized report
current_report_observation.does_not_prove: that the test run completed - a failing test suite still produces a complete Clover report

upstream_exit_semantics.known: a non-zero exit from pest/phpunit means TEST FAILURES OR ERRORS, not a failed coverage measurement. The runner is written on that basis: it keeps the status separate and still accepts a finalized Clover report. Established from shipped code.
upstream_exit_semantics.unknown: the precise code table for the pinned pest/phpunit version
upstream_exit_semantics.missing_source: no composer.lock / package-lock.json in this repository: these are consumer-side dev dependencies, so no pinned version exists here whose documented exit table could be cited

producers.normative_completion_requirement: Coverage completion is a property of the CLOVER REPORT being finalized, not of the test-runner exit status. C2 must observe the process to detect a kill or timeout that truncated Clover, while keeping the test-failure signal on its own gate.

timeout_handling.note: a timeout kill would truncate Clover; the non-empty check catches an empty file but not a truncated one

report_finalization_condition.missing: a check that the Clover document is well-formed and complete rather than truncated

analyzed_scope_identity.note: the Clover report names the files measured, but the scope is not digested into the evidence

record_report_binding.required: sha256 of the normalized report as written, plus the backend actually selected (pest or phpunit)

no_observation_behavior.matrix: unobserved -> never valid-clean; findings surface as valid-findings-unobserved

producers.residual_gap: The captured exit status is discarded before the evidence layer, and the selected backend is not recorded.

producers.backend_selection: the package.json script 'test:coverage' then 'coverage', run through the detected package manager. The BACKEND IS THE CONSUMER'S SCRIPT and is not knowable from this repository.

current_process_observation.mechanism: the package-manager invocation ends in `|| true`

current_report_observation.condition: an Istanbul json-summary exists and is non-empty; the runner clears any stale summary FIRST so a previous run cannot be normalized as current evidence

upstream_exit_semantics.reason: the backend is an arbitrary consumer-defined npm script, so there is no exit table to cite
upstream_exit_semantics.missing_source: by construction - the script is defined in the adopter's package.json

producers.normative_completion_requirement: An observed outcome for the consumer's script, plus the identity of the script actually run. Completion is a property of the Istanbul summary being finalized, not of the script's exit status.

report_finalization_condition.missing: a completeness check on the summary document

record_report_binding.required: sha256 of the normalized report as written, plus the script name actually executed
